summary: Our team "CIA" made the game "DUSTFALL". It gives players a chance to expereince a fun and interactive mission on MARS and also simultaniosly learn about flaura and fauna on martian terrain, navigation, weather forecasting and most importantly collaboration amongst teamates that need leadership and guidence from you as a player. Furthermore, DUSTFALL also simulates real weather conditions on MARS, which means that survival is essntial for the mission to succeed, this includes delegating the tasks to your team efficiently and accordingly for the longevity of the team's mission. This means that the students will learn decision making on the first hand and what to prioritise under pressure to ensure survival of the group and the completion of the mission.
details:
DUSTFALL Details

Our game "DUSTFALL" is a highly interactive MARS survival game, where the main goal of the game is to survive the harsh conditions of MARS whilst balancing limited resources and scarced supplies. DUSTFALL is not only interactive but also provides students with basic understanding of flaura and fauna on martian terrain, navigation, weather forcating and most importantly leadership, additionally students are exposing themselves to an overview of basic enginering and decision making through our game. Furthermore we intend to help students make use of their time spent on a device more educational, whilst still giving the dopamaine and engagingness of a normal game, at the same time helping students learn real world skills that become second nature. As for "DUSTFALL" the game itself we used the GODOT game engine and GDscript for the main code. Also, assistance from Gemini was much needed to help create a general outline of my team's creative ideas. Additionally, much of the assets were made in Prisma3D and some were cherry picked form NASA themselves to ensure pricision. Personally "DUSTFALL" is different because it strives on it's storyline and the general ability of the player himself instead of a structured gameplay, which means multiple outcomes are possible depending on each student's ability to manage their team. Our team also took into consideration the true conditions on MARS wether it is weather or terrain, so that it is accurate and on point. Subsequently, we also put in much consideration into the user interface to ensure players have the best experience possible. Lastly, we made sure that our game was educational enough so that each and every student can experience and learn about the many skills that can be beneficial for expanding their knowledge.
